headline.text: Itä-Uusimaa's crude share of recorded multidisciplinary team meetings is 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–1.4; n=0/272) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, which measures recording practice, not care.

details.text: For multidisciplinary team meetings, the 95% confidence interval for Itä-Uusimaa's crude share of 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–1.4; n=0/272) excludes the national value of 6.0% (893/14873), reflecting that HILMO records procedures only from direct patient contacts and therefore measures recording practice, not care.

Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can receive several treatments, Itä-Uusimaa's crude shares are not distinguishable from national values, as every 95% confidence interval includes the national benchmark: curative 28.3% (95% CI 23.3–33.9; n=77/272) versus 27.0% (4009/14873), life-prolonging 30.1% (95% CI 25.0–35.9; n=82/272) versus 30.4% (4522/14873), and symptomatic 36.8% (95% CI 31.3–42.6; n=100/272) versus 39.5% (5871/14873).

Itä-Uusimaa's crude share of patients with no treatment record within 12 months is 31.6% (95% CI 26.4–37.4; n=86/272) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, where the 95% confidence interval includes the national value and the category mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded.

While county wait times are not in the public report, preliminary, unpublished national figures show lung cancer takes 155 days on average from symptoms to treatment in Finland (56 days patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care), compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark.

headline.text: County treatment shares in the public table are crude, lacking age adjustment and stage adjustment, while public data do not capture pre-diagnostic pathway timestamps.

details.text: Taulukko 11 gives crude county shares with separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted—county age-adjusted shares appear only by sex in Kuva 16, with digitised national curative lines at 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women (about ±0.5 percentage points)—and separately they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article reports that HILMO hospital discharge diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, supporting diagnosis concordance, whereas lung cancer data reporting, collection and storage remain incomplete and Finland has no cancer quality registry.

Public report data do not measure symptom onset or referrals, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned at all, and imaging appears only indirectly as the diagnosis basis in approximately 20% of patients without imaging dates or waits.

In specialist care, the public report records whether a lung cancer visit appears in HILMO within 12 months (93.6% nationally, using visits up to 3 months before diagnosis to start follow-up) and which treatment type occurs within 12 months, but not when visits or treatments occur.

headline.text: The team recommends publishing how completely key fields are recorded, reporting access times using THL 21/2016 definitions with handover alerts, and adopting a KYS-style referral template and diagnostic contact.

details.text: Because Itä-Uusimaa's crude multidisciplinary team recording share is 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–1.4; n=0/272) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients nationally, the team recommends publishing per county how completely stage, drug treatment and multidisciplinary team meetings are recorded as data-quality signals, alongside uniform recording instructions.

Since the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and national access-time monitoring is lacking, the team recommends reporting referral-to-treatment access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions (for 16 cancers) with handover alerts, while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Given mentor insight that a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating in specialist care, and because KYS's regional pathway document provides a referral template and instructs referring persistent unexplained symptoms even if the X-ray is clear, the team recommends adopting a KYS-style referral template and a persistent-symptoms primary-care referral rule.

Because no reviewed regional pathway document names a contact person for the diagnostic phase, the team recommends naming a diagnostic-phase contact person from referral to diagnosis, while the STM roadmap (measure 1.2.3) plans guidance on a named care-coordinator model by 2026–2028 for counties to adopt by 2029–2031.

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
